references.text: Noah sends out the dove to see if the water has receded from the surface of the earth – the immediate context for the sending of the dove.
Noah sends out the dove again; the second time it returns with an olive leaf, the third time it does not return – the development after the dove initially found no rest.
The waters stood over the earth for one hundred and fifty days, which explains why the dove could find no resting place for its foot.
Almost word-for-word parallel: 'You shall not find rest for your foot' (לא תמצא מנוח לכף רגלך), the same expression used about the dove in Gen 8:9.
The psalmist wishes to have wings like a dove, to fly away and find rest – a thematic parallel to the dove's search for a resting place.
The dove that builds its nest at the edge of the cliff – a thematic parallel with the dove seeking a place to rest.
Peter refers to Noah and the eight who were saved through water, a New Testament connection to the flood narrative.
